jamie: heads up — seeing a weird pattern of tiny leftover gpu pods piling up in ap-southeast-2; many nodes show 0.25/1 gpus reserved and scheduling refuses to pack larger jobs, cluster looks fragmented
sara: ugh, same region? any taints/affinity spikes in the recent rollout? :thinking_face:
jamie: ap-southeast-2, yes. no big taint changes per changelog. noticed a lot of pods with nodeAffinity requiredDuringScheduling ignoring soft affinity, and fractional fractional-gpu requests from inference-lite jobs
lee: fractional requests + strict anti-affinity = perfect fragmentation storm. can you paste kubectl get pods -o wide for a few examples?
jamie: pasted a snippet from one node
jamie: ```
NAME                      READY STATUS   CPU   GPU
inference-lite-rc-7k9bz   1/1   Running   100m  0.25
transformer-batch-2       0/1   Pending   4     1
```
jamie: node has 0.75 GPU free according to metrics-server but scheduler won't pack the 1 GPU pod
nate: likely lease/accounting granularity — we use fractional allocations tracked in internal metastore, but some kubelets report rounding down. scheduler sees available <1 because KV cache uses floor rounding at 2 decimal places
sara: can we verify with node-exporter/telemetry? show the raw allocatable vs used GPU from NVIDIADevices on that node
jamie: gathered metrics: allocatable 8.00, used 7.25 according to agent; kubelet summary shows 7.3; internal metadata ledger shows 7.1
lee: consistent with small race/rounding differences. that explains 0.7 vs 0.75 mismatches — scheduler conservatively rejects 1 GPU pods when free <1.0 by threshold
nish: long term we should make scheduler tolerant (allow epsilon packing) or coalesce fractional requests when below threshold. but need immediate mitigation for tail latency and cost
sara: options: 1) run a descheduler cron to agglomerate tiny pods onto fewer nodes, 2) temporarily relax scheduling predicate to allow near-fit placement, 3) bump warm pool for 1g jobs in that AZ
jamie: descheduler could be low-risk short-term. we have a descheduler job in eng-infra, can trigger for ap-southeast-2 only
nate: note: descheduler will evict some inference-lite pods => potential 10-20% QPS blip. ops-oncall ok with short spike? @ops-oncall
ops-oncall: ok to proceed during off-peak window 01:00-03:00 UTC. monitor model latency closely
lee: patch idea: scheduler allowPredicates: allowOvercommitEpsilon: 0.05 — gives 5% tolerance. PR ready as proof-of-concept: https://git.internal/r/redwood/sched/merge/PR-412
sara: we need canary on non-prod first. Also add a metric alert for packable_pods_rejected_count to catch regressions
jamie: quick manual workaround: cordon a few high-usage nodes and drain small pods to consolidate them; commands:
jamie: ```bash
kubectl get nodes -l az=ap-southeast-2a -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.status.allocatable.gpu != null) | .metadata.name' | xargs -I{} kubectl cordon {}
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='app=inference-lite'
```
nish: careful with drain flags, prefer descheduler unless we have explicit no-downtime agreement
lee: cost note — fragmented nodes cause ~12% wasted GPU hours last week in that cluster per cost dashboard
sara: can we push a short-term autoscaler tweak: prefer provisioning of 1g racks rather than fractional flavor in that AZ? makes packing simpler but increases cold-start cost
nate: we can change autoscaler config via feature flag: autoscaler.default_gpu_unit = 1.0 for ap-southeast-2; quick toggle, rollbackable
